claims.claim: DeepSeek-R1 beats OpenAI's o1 on the benchmarks AIME, MATH-500, and SWE-bench Verified.
R1 is available on Hugging Face under an MIT license, meaning it can be used commercially without restrictions.
DeepSeek released distilled versions of R1 ranging from 1.5 billion to 70 billion parameters.
The full R1 is available through DeepSeek's API at prices 90%-95% cheaper than OpenAI's o1.
The smallest distilled version of R1 can run on a laptop.

delta: open weights (MIT) vs o1's closed API-only

prior_art.name: o1
prior_art.differs: R1 is open-weight (MIT license) and available via API at significantly lower cost; o1 is closed and API-only. R1 reports slightly higher scores on AIME, MATH-500, and SWE-bench Verified in self-reported benchmarks.

prior_art.name: AIME
prior_art.differs: R1 evaluated on AIME 2024 with self-reported score of 79.8; used as benchmark for reasoning models.

prior_art.name: MATH-500
prior_art.differs: R1 evaluated on MATH-500 with self-reported score of 97.3; used to assess mathematical reasoning.

prior_art.name: SWE-bench Verified
prior_art.differs: R1 evaluated on SWE-bench Verified with self-reported score of 49.2; used to test code generation and problem-solving in real GitHub issues.

parsed.recheck_when: independent benchmark results on AIME, MATH-500, or SWE-bench Verified are published
parsed.tldr: DeepSeek released an open-weight, MIT-licensed reasoning model with 671B parameters, available via API at 90-95% lower cost than OpenAI's o1, with self-reported SOTA scores on key reasoning benchmarks.
